answer: The Winter War ended with the Moscow Peace Treaty, signed on 13 March 1940, after Finland's military position on the Karelian Isthmus became dire and Finnish commander-in-chief Mannerheim urged a peace deal [1]. Under the treaty Finland ceded 9% of its territory to the Soviet Union, but it retained its sovereignty [1]. Hostilities ceased on 13 March 1940, after the Finns had proposed an armistice on 6 March and the Soviets had pressed further demands [1][3].

facts.text: The Winter War ended with the Moscow Peace Treaty on 13 March 1940.

facts.text: Finland ceded 9% of its territory to the Soviet Union in the Moscow Peace Treaty.
facts.source_sentence: Hostilities ceased in March 1940 with the signing of the Moscow Peace Treaty in which Finland ceded 9% of its territory to the Soviet Union.

facts.text: Finnish commander-in-chief Mannerheim urged a peace deal because the Finnish army was near the breaking point.
facts.source_sentence: Consequently, Finnish commander-in-chief Carl Gustaf Emil Mannerheim urged a peace deal with the Soviets, while the Finns still retained bargaining power.

facts.text: Finland retained its sovereignty and enhanced its international reputation.
facts.source_sentence: Finland retained its sovereignty and enhanced its international reputation.

facts.text: The Finns proposed an armistice on 6 March, but the Soviets declined the offer.
facts.source_sentence: The Finns proposed an armistice on 6 March, but the Soviets, wanting to keep the pressure on the Finnish government, declined the offer.

milestones.answer: The Winter War ended with the Moscow Peace Treaty, signed on 13 March 1940, after it became clear that Finland's ability to defend itself was much better than expected. Finland lost Salla, south-eastern Finland, the outer islands of the Gulf of Finland and the western part of Kalastajansaarento, and also had to lease Hanko to the Soviet Union for military purposes.

facts.text: The Moscow Peace Treaty was concluded on 13 March 1940, when it became clear that Finland's ability to defend itself was much better than expected.
facts.source_sentence: Moskovan rauha solmittiin 13. maaliskuuta 1940, kun valkeni, että Suomen kyky puolustautua oli paljon odotettua parempi.

facts.text: As a result of the war, Finland lost Salla, south-eastern Finland, the outer islands of the Gulf of Finland and the western part of Kalastajansaarento.
facts.source_sentence: Sodan seurauksena Suomi menetti Sallan, Kaakkois-Suomen, Suomenlahden ulkosaaret ja Kalastajansaarennon länsiosan.

facts.text: Finland also had to lease Hanko to the Soviet Union for military purposes.
facts.source_sentence: Suomi joutui myös vuokraamaan Neuvostoliitolle Hangon sotilaallisiin tarkoituksiin.

milestones.answer: The Winter War ended with the Moscow Peace Treaty, which was signed and took effect on 13 March 1940. Finland ceded about 10 percent of its territory, including Viipuri (Vyborg), its second-largest city, to the Soviet Union, and had to lease Hanko for military use.

milestones.answer: The Winter War ended with the Moscow Peace Treaty, signed on 12 March 1940 and taking effect the next day; Finland ceded about 10 percent of its territory, including Viipuri (Vyborg), its second largest city, to the Soviet Union, and had to lease Hanko to the Soviets.

facts.text: Finland ceded 10 percent of its territory and its second largest city, Viipuri, to the Soviet Union.
facts.source_sentence: Sota päättyi Moskovan rauhansopimukseen, jossa Suomi luovutti 10 prosenttia maa-alueistaan ja toiseksi suurimman kaupunkinsa, Viipurin, Neuvostoliitolle.

facts.text: The Moscow Peace Treaty was signed on the evening of 12 March 1940, and fighting on the front ended the next day.
facts.source_sentence: Moskovan rauhansopimus allekirjoitettiin illalla 12. maaliskuuta 1940. Taistelutoiminta rintamilla päättyi seuraavana päivänä asteittain klo 11 alkaen.

facts.text: Finland had to lease Hanko to the Soviet Union as a military base for 30 years.
facts.source_sentence: Suomi joutui myös vuokraamaan Hangon Neuvostoliitolle tukikohdaksi 30 vuodeksi ja rakentamaan Kantalahden ja Sallan välille rautatien.

milestones.answer: The Winter War ended with the Moscow Peace Treaty, signed on the evening of 12 March 1940, after which fighting on the front ceased the next day. Finland ceded about ten percent of its territory, including Viipuri, and had to lease Hanko to the Soviet Union.
